The glossary defines a care coordinator as a person, but here it labels the intermediary's system, which creates and posts the CP Task; the glossary calls that system the coordination platform, as every other intermediary diagram does.
The coordination platform's acronym is run into 'Task'; every other line in this diagram writes 'CP Task'.

The glossary makes the self-referral referral source the organization running the community resource referral platform (the coordination platform), not the person; this actor creates, posts and polls Tasks, so it is the platform the individual uses.
The person referring themselves is the subject of care, which the glossary calls the patient.
The glossary's term for these validated instruments is standardized assessment instrument.
'Screening' names the assessment activity; STU 3.0 moved to assessment wording and the glossary has no 'screening' entry. This is Gravity-authored artwork, not an external name.

dismissed.reason: 'Authorized Individual' is the patient's representative, not the subject of care, so 'patient' would change the meaning.

glossary_feedback.observation: The glossary has no term for a person authorized to act on the patient's behalf. The self-referral diagram says 'Authorized Individual' and the self-referral page says 'authorized representative', so neither can be checked against a definition.
